::Personal opinions abound here: There have been ''a lot'' of discussions about "commit suicide", and there's never been a consensus to change the language simply to suit one's own preferences or the possibility that style manuals in general may avoid the phrasing. I do think, however, that changing the wording just for the sake of changing it reinforces false beliefs about the phrasing (for instance, that "commit" is inherently negative wording; one can "commit" to becoming a better person, for instance). Frankly, if you're seriously bothered by it, you can start a discussion at the article's Talk page and we can have another go-round on it, but I'd encourage you not to do so. The current wording is stable, and as such, it shouldn't be changed just for the sake of change. However, if you were going to change it, frankly I prefer wording like "killed himself/herself" to "died by suicide" which to me just sounds like a ridiculous way to avoid saying "committed suicide". I hope this is helpful. I appreciate that editors who change the wording have good intentions, but I'm tired of seeing the word "committed" inappropriately stigmatized as well. [[User:Doniago|DonIago]] ([[User talk:Doniago|talk]]) 13:07, 31 July 2026 (UTC)

::::I honestly don't agree with your assessment that the word "commit" paints suicide in any sort of light, because I don't think the word has any inherently positive or negative connotations, but our opinions on this obviously differ, and that difference, painted broadly, is one of the reasons why the MoS doesn't currently have a prohibition against using the word. As for your point about suicide being the only cause of death that's "committed"...that's because it's the only one I'm readily aware of where the person is (typically?) engaging in an intentional action...though people can and have committed to other forms of self-harm...but again, that doesn't make the word "commit" inherently negative; it's the words that follow it that are negative.
::::I have ''a lot'' of reservations about changing the phrasing at all, because the more we vanish it the more we imply that it ''should'' be vanished, and I '''do not''' agree with that. However, as we're only discussing a single article, in the spirit of compromise, if you feel very strongly about it, I'll accept "killed himself". But I would '''urge''' you to please read the prior discussions regarding this and familiarize yourself with the reasons why other editors are also opposed to prohibiting the phrase. It's very possible they've articulated the concerns more clearly than I have, and if we're going to engage in [[WP:CENSOR|censorship]], we should at least have a good understanding of why we're doing so, from both sides of the argument. Wikipedia does have functionality for adding footnotes (see ''[[Inception]]''), but those are generally intended to be explanatory, and any statements that involved claims would still need sourcing. This may, for better or worse, just be considered a situation where sources haven't tended to point it out because they feel it's so obvious there's no need to point it out. Unfortunately, that works against us. An author pointing out that they weren't happy that a work used the name of their book but was otherwise unrelated would be a great source if it exists. ''[[Starship Troopers (film)]]'' might be the best-case scenario for what something like this could look like, where there's a lot of information available on which of the folks behind the film actually read the novel and what they chose to adapt and why, etc. Unfortunately I imagine most film adaptations of books never really get this depth of behind-the-scenes material for us to work with. items.post_text: ::Personal opinions abound here: There have been ''a lot'' of discussions about "commit suicide", and there's never been a consensus to change the language simply to suit one's own preferences or the possibility that style manuals in general may avoid the phrasing. I do think, however, that changing the wording just for the sake of changing it reinforces false beliefs about the phrasing (for instance, that "commit" is inherently negative wording; one can "commit" to becoming a better person, for instance). Frankly, if you're seriously bothered by it, you can start a discussion at the article's Talk page and we can have another go-round on it, but I'd encourage you not to do so. The current wording is stable, and as such, it shouldn't be changed just for the sake of change. However, if you were going to change it, frankly I prefer wording like "killed himself/herself" to "died by suicide" which to me just sounds like a ridiculous way to avoid saying "committed suicide". I hope this is helpful. I appreciate that editors who change the wording have good intentions, but I'm tired of seeing the word "committed" inappropriately stigmatized as well. [[User:Doniago|DonIago]] ([[User talk:Doniago|talk]]) 13:07, 31 July 2026 (UTC)

::::I honestly don't agree with your assessment that the word "commit" paints suicide in any sort of light, because I don't think the word has any inherently positive or negative connotations, but our opinions on this obviously differ, and that difference, painted broadly, is one of the reasons why the MoS doesn't currently have a prohibition against using the word. As for your point about suicide being the only cause of death that's "committed"...that's because it's the only one I'm readily aware of where the person is (typically?) engaging in an intentional action...though people can and have committed to other forms of self-harm...but again, that doesn't make the word "commit" inherently negative; it's the words that follow it that are negative.
::::I have ''a lot'' of reservations about changing the phrasing at all, because the more we vanish it the more we imply that it ''should'' be vanished, and I '''do not''' agree with that. However, as we're only discussing a single article, in the spirit of compromise, if you feel very strongly about it, I'll accept "killed himself". But I would '''urge''' you to please read the prior discussions regarding this and familiarize yourself with the reasons why other editors are also opposed to prohibiting the phrase. It's very possible they've articulated the concerns more clearly than I have, and if we're going to engage in [[WP:CENSOR|censorship]], we should at least have a good understanding of why we're doing so, from both sides of the argument. [[User:Doniago|DonIago]] ([[User talk:Doniago|talk]]) 03:18, 1 August 2026 (UTC)

== July 2026 ==

[[File:Information.svg|25px|alt=Information icon]] Hello, I'm [[User:Doniago|Doniago]]. I noticed that you added or changed content in an article, [[:Fantastic Mr. Fox (film)]], but you didn't provide a [[Wikipedia:Reliable sources|reliable source]]. On Wikipedia, it's important that article content be [[Wikipedia:Verifiability|verifiable]]. If you'd like to resubmit your change [[Wikipedia:Citing sources|with a citation]], your edit is archived in [[Special:History/Fantastic Mr. Fox (film)|the page history]]. If you have any questions, you can leave me a message on [[User talk:Doniago|my talk page]]. ''Please do not claim a film is a box-office bomb nor link to that article without providing a source that has made that claim.'' <!-- Template:uw-unsourced1 --> [[User:Doniago|DonIago]] ([[User talk:Doniago|talk]]) 19:25, 13 July 2026 (UTC)

::Wikipedia articles can't cite other Wikipedia articles as sources per [[WP:CIRCULAR]]; among other things, the linked article could change in a way that rendered the claim no longer substantiated. What you can do is pull a source from the other article and re-use it (i.e. both articles would cite the same external source).
::Unfortunately we don't have any way to keep links from going stale, so if you're getting 404s on what should be good links, it would be awesome if you could update them (and check to make sure that the linked articles do claim that they're "natural horror" films, if you're there anyway).
::While AllMovie isn't an optimal source (AFI or BFI would be better), it certainly isn't akin to [[WP:IMDB|IMDb]], as far as I understand things.
::We're adding sources to establish that the movie has in fact been classified as a "natural horror" film; it's existence is good to know but insufficient for inclusion on the list.
::Happy editing! [[User:Doniago|DonIago]] ([[User talk:Doniago|talk]]) 15:42, 10 August 2026 (UTC)

:It's not a matter of what I want you to do. [[WP:IPCV]] stipulates that references to "in popular culture" must have their significance demonstrated, which is best done by providing a [[WP:SECONDARY|secondary]] source. Whether or not the references exist isn't the point; the point is whether any reliable sources took note of them. Otherwise the page for ''[[Citizen Kane]]'' would be littered with all kinds of trival mentions of every time anyone said "Rosebud". 
:Hope this is helpful! [[User:Doniago|DonIago]] ([[User talk:Doniago#top|talk]]) 19:24, 7 October 2026 (UTC)
